main_body: Tall brick shopfront building: mansard slate roof with dormers and chimney, orange cornice, two brick storeys with lit windows, balcony, striped awning and shop windows
top_band: Slate-blue roof slope with a lighter grey-teal flat roof panel above it, rows ~10-41, ending at the orange cornice (rows 42-45)
evidence: Reading down the centre column: the grey-teal roof panel and slate slope (rows ~10-41) are a clear roof surface, about 20 rows. The orange cornice (rows 42-45) acts as the front-edge line, with a dark shadow row just under it. The brick face (rows 46-112) and shopfront (rows 113-141) follow. Windows have projecting sills and lintels, and the balcony and awning step out from the wall. The facade itself is mostly frontal, like the reference houses, but the roof slope is a distinct visible top, so it reads as 3/4 and not a bare elevation with a hat.

style.evidence: The brick is shaded in several reds with individual bricks and mortar. The slate has stone-like scallop texture in 4-5 blue-greys. The window glow is speckled in orange and yellow. The awning and shop details are detailed too. Outlines are dark brown beside brick and dark blue-grey beside slate, not pure black. Tile density is as high as or higher than the reference houses. No large flat fills, apart from the narrow orange cornice and the dark band under the balcony.
